sections.overview: Elysia chlorotica is an eastern North American sacoglossan sea slug in genus Elysia.
sections.identification: Its vivid green, flattened body holds chloroplasts acquired from algae.
sections.habitat: It lives in shallow salt and tidal marshes, creeks and pools along the western Atlantic coast.
sections.diet: It feeds on Vaucheria algae and sequesters their chloroplasts rather than digesting every plastid.
sections.behavior: The retained kleptoplasts can continue photosynthesizing for months inside cells lining its digestive branches.
sections.reproduction: It is a simultaneous hermaphrodite with both reproductive systems in one individual.
sections.ecology: Related Elysia timida also retains plastids, but obtains them from a different alga.
sections.conservation: Animal Diversity Web reports no special status in the conservation lists it summarizes.
